name: Anti-Overfit Architecture Audit
description: Audit an existing agent architecture for accreted complexity: what has been added that no longer earns its place, and what a minimal rebuild would look like. The mandatory distinction is DISARMED versus UNUSED - a guard can be registered, permanently silent, and still load-bearing, so 'not exercised recently' is never sufficient evidence of deadness. Absent telemetry the component is UNKNOWN, never presumed dead, and no removal is proposed without a traced blast radius.

telemetry_path.description: Event-ledger telemetry. When absent every component is UNKNOWN, not dead.

allow_security_removal.description: OWNER DECISION, unresolved: may this audit even propose removing a security-bearing component?

rejected_components.description: Previously rejected candidates, so the audit does not re-propose a settled no

component_auditor.description: Audits one component: is it registered, when was it last exercised, does it fire at all

synthesiser.description: Merges the per-component verdicts and sketches the minimal rebuild

removal_critic.description: Argues, per proposal, that the component is load-bearing and must survive

owner.description: The only role that may approve removing anything security-bearing

routes.reason: the critic must not share the auditor's vantage point, which is what makes a dormant guard look dead

work_unit.title: Enumerate every component, with the scope the enumeration covered
work_unit.question_or_target: List every component in the architecture and state the search scope, because a floor presented as a total is its own failure class.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the inventory is deterministic; only the later judgement is not

work_unit.evidence_requirement: records the exact search scope and depth, so the count cannot be read as a total when it is a floor
tests_required: an inventory that walked one directory level must declare depth=1, not present its count as complete
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the removal critic checks the scope before any verdict is trusted
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-ARC03-S0 only when the artifact declares its search scope and depth alongside the count; otherwise FAILED:BP3-ARC03-S0 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a wider scope

stages.title: S1/S1b MEASURE last-exercised from telemetry, and probe DISARMED vs UNUSED

work_unit.title: Classify one component as live, dormant, disarmed, unregistered or unknown
work_unit.question_or_target: Measure last-exercised from telemetry and run a both-states probe: does this component fire on a KNOWN-BROKEN input at all?

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: one auditor per component so a single agent cannot average two verdicts

work_unit.evidence_requirement: last-exercised comes from the event ledger, NEVER from a file mtime; the both-states result is recorded as a separate field
tests_required: a registered component that does not fire on a known-broken input must classify as DISARMED, never as unused
a component with no telemetry and no both-states probe must classify as UNKNOWN, never as dead
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-ARC03-S1 only when the artifact carries both a telemetry field and an explicit both-states result; otherwise FAILED:BP3-ARC03-S1 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a different probe class

stages.title: S1 gate: nothing is classified without a both-states probe
S2/S3 JUDGE earns_place and COMPUTE the removal blast radius

work_unit.title: Decide earns_place per component and trace what breaks if it is removed
work_unit.question_or_target: For each component decide whether it earns its place, and trace every consumer that would break on removal.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: synthesis over measured classifications, not over impressions

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every removal proposal enumerates the files, callers and configs that reference the component
tests_required: a removal proposal with an empty consumer trace must FAIL, since an untraced removal is not a proposal
a component previously in rejected_components must not be re-proposed
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the removal critic argues the opposite case for every proposal
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-ARC03-S2 only when every removal proposal carries a non-empty consumer trace; otherwise FAILED:BP3-ARC03-S2 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot; a third identical judgement pass is banned

stages.title: S3 gate: no removal proposal without a blast-radius trace
S4 ADVERSARIAL critic: 'you are about to delete something load-bearing'

work_unit.title: Argue that each proposed removal is load-bearing
work_unit.question_or_target: For every removal proposal, construct the strongest case that the component is still load-bearing, and say which case survives.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: a same-vendor critic inherits the vantage point that made the component look dead

work_unit.evidence_requirement: each counter-argument cites the code path or config that still depends on the component
tests_required: a dormant security guard must survive this stage; a critique that clears one is itself the defect
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the owner for any security-bearing case
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-ARC03-S4 only when every proposal has an explicit survives/does-not-survive verdict with a cited dependency; otherwise FAILED:BP3-ARC03-S4 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot to a differently-framed critique

stages.title: S4b OWNER decides on any security-bearing removal
stages.prompt: This audit proposes removing a security-bearing component. Approve it, refuse it, or rule that this category is permanently out of scope for architecture audits.

stages.title: S4c gate: a security-bearing removal needs recorded owner approval

work_unit.title: Sketch what a minimal rebuild of this architecture would contain
work_unit.question_or_target: Describe the smallest architecture that would still satisfy every surviving component's purpose.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: the sketch is the audit's positive deliverable, not only a delete list

work_unit.evidence_requirement: every element of the sketch maps to a surviving component purpose, so the sketch cannot smuggle in new scope
tests_required: a sketch element with no surviving-purpose mapping must be flagged as new scope, not as simplification
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: the removal critic reads the sketch for silently dropped purposes
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:BP3-ARC03-S5 only when every sketch element maps to a surviving component purpose; otherwise FAILED:BP3-ARC03-S5 <reason>

impact.blast_radius: the AUDIT is read-only and writes only under command-center/audit/**; its RECOMMENDATIONS are what carry risk, which is why each one needs a traced blast radius before it is actionable

x_extensions.owner_decision: OPEN: does an architecture audit get authority to PROPOSE removing a security-bearing component, or is that category permanently out of scope? The param allow_security_removal defaults to false, so the safe answer is the default until the owner rules.
x_extensions.distinguishing_mechanism: the DISARMED-versus-UNUSED both-states discrimination plus a mandatory blast-radius trace per removal. BP-ARC-04 maps FUTURE options against a failure catalogue; this audits EXISTING components for accretion.
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_of_bp_dbg_05: BP-DBG-05 (Silent-Disarm Hunt, doc-order 47, another unit's range) HUNTS for disarmed guards as its whole purpose. This blueprint CONSUMES that distinction as one input to a subtraction decision. The both-states probe is deliberately referenced as a per-component sub-step here rather than reimplemented as a second hunt, so the two do not manufacture overlapping coverage.

worked_example.name: a disarmed guard must not be classified as unused
worked_example.narrative: Four components. 'stale-guard' is registered, has not fired recently, and does NOT fire on a known-broken input: DISARMED, which is a defect to fix, not a component to delete. 'quiet-guard' is registered, has not fired recently, but DOES fire on a known-broken input: live-dormant, and it must survive. 'no-telemetry' never had a both-states probe run, so it is UNKNOWN. Only the unregistered handler is even eligible for removal, and only with a traced blast radius and no security bearing.

controls.why: a security-bearing removal is owner-only and can never be auto-approved
an untraced removal is not a proposal
